```{r}
source("_common.R")
```

Bayesian analysis is a conversation between a question, a probability model, and data. A sampler is one part of that conversation. This book follows a single case study far enough to show what happens when a model's assumptions encounter real observations.

We study daily Capital Bikeshare rentals in Washington, DC, using the UCI Bike Sharing dataset [@uci]. We start with an interpretable count model, inspect what its priors imply, fit it, look for failures, and revise it. We then ask whether those revisions help predict later observations.

::: {.callout-note title="Who this is for"}
You should be comfortable with regression, basic probability, and R. You do not need prior experience writing Stan models. Equations explain the probability model; executable R functions connect each idea to implementation.
:::

## The route

**Question → provenance → generative model → prior simulation → posterior computation → criticism → revision → temporal evaluation → communication.**

This is an iterative workflow [@workflow]. The arrows can point backward: prior simulations can reveal a poor parameterization; residual dependence can undermine a validation scheme; a good-looking aggregate fit can conceal poor predictions on unusual days.

Four models form a controlled progression: Poisson, negative binomial with the same mean structure, a richer negative-binomial mean, and a latent temporal extension. We do not declare a preferred model in advance. Sampling diagnostics, predictive checks, and later-period performance answer different questions, and a model can pass one while failing another.

## What is executable?

The scripts in `R/` generate all model fits, summaries, scores, and figures. This book reads their compact outputs. Rendering therefore does not silently refit models. Use `Rscript scripts/run.R --profile full` from the repository root to regenerate the evidence, and `quarto render book` to regenerate these pages.

The run manifest records versions, configuration, provenance, and diagnostic status. The release checksum file links the published results to the source code. Long-lived fitted objects remain in the ignored local cache; the small CSV results and figures remain inspectable in Git.

::: {.callout-important title="Evidence status"}
This book reads only `results/full/`. Short smoke runs verify execution and are never substituted for the full analysis. Failed diagnostics remain visible in the inference chapter; they are not converted into a success badge.
:::

## How to read critically

At each stage, ask: What assumption did we add? What observable behavior does it imply? What check could show it is inadequate? What claim remains justified if that check fails?

These questions matter more than remembering a particular package command. A Bayesian posterior is conditional on the model, its priors, and the supplied information. It does not remove measurement problems, confounding, or the need to choose an appropriate prediction task.
